questions.question: In what order must the lifts be performed?
questions.ruleQuote: The International Powerlifting Federation recognizes the following lifts which must be taken in the same sequence in all competitions conducted under IPF rules: A. Squat B. Bench Press C. Deadlift D. Total

questions.question: Which light colour indicates a good lift?
questions.ruleQuote: Each referee will control a white and a red light. The white light indicates a “good lift,” and the red light indicates a “no lift.”

questions.question: How deep must the lifter go for a good squat?
options: Top of the legs at the hip joint below the top of the knees
Top of the thighs parallel to the floor at the lowest point
Hip crease level with the top of the kneecap
A knee angle of ninety degrees or less
questions.ruleQuote: Upon receiving the Chief Referee’s signal, the lifter must bend the knees and lower the body until the top surface of the legs at the hip joint is lower than the top of the knees.

questions.question: How many spotter/loaders may be on the platform at any time?
questions.ruleQuote: Not more than five and not less than two spotter/loaders shall be on the platform at any time. The Referees may decide the number of spotter/loaders required on the platform at any time 2, 3, 4, or 5.

questions.question: How many weight changes are permitted on the third-attempt deadlift?
questions.ruleQuote: In the third round of the deadlift, two changes are permitted. The change of the weight may be higher or lower than the lifters previously submitted third attempt.

questions.question: How many attempts does each lifter get on each lift?
questions.ruleQuote: Each competitor is allowed three attempts on each lift.

questions.question: What is the maximum width of a lifting belt?
questions.ruleQuote: Width of belt maximum 10 cm.

questions.question: What must remain in contact with the bench during the bench press?
options: The entire back and the buttocks
questions.ruleQuote: The lifter must lie on their back with the head, shoulders, and buttocks … in contact with the bench surface.

questions.question: What command does the Chief Referee give to start the deadlift?

ruleReference.subsection: Signals required for the three lifts

questions.ruleQuote: [Deadlift, commencement:] No signal required. [Completion:] A visual signal consisting of a downward movement of the arm together with the audible command “down”.

questions.question: What is the maximum thickness of a knee sleeve?
questions.ruleQuote: Knee sleeves shall be of a maximum thickness of 7 mm and a maximum length of 30 cm.

questions.question: What colour must a 25 kg disc be?
questions.ruleQuote: Discs must conform to the following color code: 10 kg and under - any color, 15 kg - yellow, 20 kg - blue, 25 kg - red.

questions.question: What colour must a 10 kg disc be?
questions.ruleQuote: Discs must conform to the following color code: 10 kg and under - any color, 15 kg - yellow, 20 kg - blue, 25 kg - red.

questions.question: Excluding record attempts, what is the minimum weight increase between attempts?
questions.ruleQuote: Unless attempts are made on records, in Squat, Bench Press and Deadlift, the progression must be at least 2.5 kg between all attempts

questions.question: In a record attempt, by how much must the bar exceed the current record?
questions.ruleQuote: In a record attempt the weight of the barbell must be at least 0.5 kg in excess of the current record.

questions.question: In the squat, must the lifter's thumbs wrap around the bar?
options: No, but they must remain in contact with the bar
Yes, a thumbs-around grip is required at all times
Yes, unless the lifter uses a low bar position
No, and they need not touch the bar at all
questions.ruleQuote: The thumbs are not required to wrap around the bar. However, the hands, thumb, and fingers must remain in complete contact with the bar or the duration of the lift.

questions.question: What is the Chief Referee's command to begin the squat?
questions.ruleQuote: The signal shall consist of a downward movement of the arm and the audible command “Squat”.

questions.question: Is a lifter required to wear a belt?
options: Yes, required for the deadlift only
Yes, required for the squat only
Yes, required for the squat and deadlift
questions.ruleQuote: Competitors may wear a belt. If worn, it shall be on the outside of the lifting suit.

questions.question: How long before the start of the competition may weigh-in begin?
questions.ruleQuote: Weighing in of the competitors must take place no earlier than two hours before the start of the competition

questions.question: In the deadlift, is foot movement after the “Down” command a cause for failure?
options: No, it is not a cause for failure
Yes, it is a cause for failure
Only if the lifter's foot is no longer flat on the floor
Only if the lifter takes a step

ruleReference.subsection: Causes for Disqualification of a Deadlift

questions.ruleQuote: Foot movement after the command “Down” will not be cause for failure.

questions.question: How many referees make up the Jury?
questions.ruleQuote: The Jury shall consist of three or five Category 1 referees.

questions.question: What is the combined weight of the bar and collars?
questions.ruleQuote: Weight of the bar and collars are to be 25 kg.

questions.question: Is the use of oil or grease on the body permitted?
options: Yes, to help fit knee sleeves
questions.ruleQuote: The use of oil, grease or other lubricants on the body, or personal equipment is strictly forbidden.

questions.question: Is the reverse grip permitted in the bench press?
options: No, the reverse grip is forbidden
Only with the Chief Referee's approval
questions.ruleQuote: The use of the reverse grip is forbidden.

questions.question: In the bench press, how far must the bar be lowered?
options: To the chest or abdominal area, elbows at or below the shoulders
To the chest or abdominal area, upper arms parallel to the floor
To the chest only, elbows at or below the shoulders
To the chest only, upper arms parallel to the floor
questions.ruleQuote: The lifter must lower the bar to the chest or abdominal area whereby the underside of both elbow joints is lowered level with or below the top surface of each respective shoulder joint

questions.question: What happens to a lifter who fails all three attempts at one lift?
options: Out of the total, but still eligible for individual lift awards
Out of the competition entirely, including all individual awards
Out of that lift only, with the total still standing
Allowed a fourth attempt at the discretion of the Jury
questions.ruleQuote: Three unsuccessful attempts in any lift will automatically eliminate the lifter from the overall competition. He may still compete for awards on individual lifts if he makes bona fide attempts on each of the lifts

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable footwear on the platform?
questions.ruleQuote: Shoes or boots shall be worn. (a) Shoes shall be taken to include only indoor sports shoes/sports boots; Weightlifting/Powerlifting boots or Deadlift slippers.

questions.question: Who officiates each lift?
options: A Chief Referee and two side referees
A Chief Referee and three side referees
A Chief Referee and one side referee
Two referees and a Jury member
questions.ruleQuote: The referees shall be three in number, the Chief Referee or Center Referee and two side referees.

questions.question: How many layers of medical tape may be worn around the thumbs?
questions.ruleQuote: Two layers of medical tape may be worn around the thumbs.

questions.question: May knee wraps and knee sleeves be worn at the same time?
options: No, the combination is strictly forbidden
Yes, provided the wraps go over the sleeves
Only with the Chief Referee's approval
questions.ruleQuote: IPF approved knee sleeves are allowed. A combination of the two is strictly forbidden.

questions.question: How must the first and heaviest discs be loaded onto the bar?
options: Face in, with the rest loaded face out
Face out, with the rest loaded face in
Either way, provided the weight is readable
questions.ruleQuote: The first and heaviest discs loaded on the bar must be loaded face in; with the rest of the discs loaded face out.
